from.place: ## Proof, step (b) Essential surjectivity: algebraization through formal glueing, specifically the torsion-extension descent used in Proposition 05ER

title: Extensions of a cyclic ideal-power quotient descend over a flat neighbourhood
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a flat map of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], let $I\subseteq R$ be a finitely generated ideal such that $R/I\to S/IS$ is an isomorphism, let $n\ge1$, and let $N$ be an $R$-module. Put $C=R/I^n$ and $C_S=C\otimes_RS$ [def-weil-module-base-change]. For every short exact sequence of $S$-modules $0\to N\otimes_RS\xrightarrow{a}T\xrightarrow{b}C_S\to0$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence], there are an exact sequence of $R$-modules $0\to N\xrightarrow{j}E\xrightarrow{q}C\to0$ and an $S$-linear isomorphism $E\otimes_RS\simeq T$ commuting with both maps from $N\otimes_RS$ and to $C_S$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 05EG (lemma-neighbourhood-extensions, line 24477), proof after 'reduce to the case where M = R/I^n': the diagram from Lemma 05EE and annihilation by Lemma 05EF

proof.text: Set $J=I^n$. It is finitely generated: if $I=(g_1,\dots,g_s)$, then $J$ is generated by the products $g_{k_1}\cdots g_{k_n}$. Choose generators $f_1,\dots,f_t$ of $J$ ($t\ge1$), so $C=R/J$. With these $f_i$ form, as in [lem-weil-pbc-cyclic-extension-cocycle], the free module $F=R^{\oplus t}$ with basis $e_i$, the quotient $M_f=F/W$ by the submodule $W$ generated by the $f_ie_j-f_je_i$, the map $\mu:M_f\to R$, $\bar e_i\mapsto f_i$ (well defined since $\mu(f_ie_j-f_je_i)=f_if_j-f_jf_i=0$, with image $J$), and $K_f=\operatorname{Ker}\mu$. Then $JK_f=0$ (Lemma 05ED): if $z=\sum_ia_i\bar e_i\in K_f$, i.e. $\sum_ia_if_i=0$, then $f_jz=\sum_ia_if_j\bar e_i=\sum_ia_if_i\bar e_j=0$ because $f_j\bar e_i=f_i\bar e_j$ in $M_f$. Hence $I^nK_f=0$ and $K_f$ is $I$-power torsion.

source.place: Lemma 05EG, proof, second paragraph: 'Let f_1, ..., f_t be generators for I^n', with Lemma 05ED (lemma-naive-Koszul-complex, line 24394) and its proof

proof.text: For an $R$-module $P$ let $Z_f(P)=\{x\in P^t: f_ix_j=f_jx_i\ \forall i,j\}$ as in [lem-weil-pbc-cyclic-extension-cocycle], $B_f(P)=\{(f_1p,\dots,f_tp):p\in P\}\subseteq Z_f(P)$ and $H_1(P)=Z_f(P)/B_f(P)$ (the group $H_1(P,f_\bullet)$ of Lemma 05EE) [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module]. Then $JH_1(N)=0$ (Lemma 05EF): for $x\in Z_f(N)$, $f_ix=(f_ix_1,\dots,f_ix_t)=(f_1x_i,\dots,f_tx_i)\in B_f(N)$. Hence $H_1(N)$ is $I$-power torsion ($I^n$ kills it).

source.place: Lemma 05EG, proof, last sentence: 'As H_1(N, f_•) is annihilated by I^n, see Lemma 05EF'; Lemma 05EF (lemma-koszul-homology-annihilated, line 24454) and its proof

proof.text: Write $f_i$ also for $\varphi(f_i)\in S$ and $P_S=P\otimes_RS$ [def-weil-module-base-change]. $Z_f(P)$ is the kernel of $\delta_P:P^t\to P^{t\times t}$, $x\mapsto(f_ix_j-f_jx_i)_{i,j}$, and $B_f(P)$ the image of $\beta_P:P\to P^t$, $p\mapsto(f_ip)_i$. Under $(P^t)_S\cong(P_S)^t$ and $(P^{t\times t})_S\cong(P_S)^{t\times t}$ [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-finite-product] the maps $\delta_N\otimes_RS$, $\beta_N\otimes_RS$ become $\delta_{N_S}$, $\beta_{N_S}$ (check on $x\otimes s$). Since $S$ is flat, tensoring the exact $0\to Z_f(N)\to N^t\xrightarrow{\delta_N}N^{t\times t}$ gives $Z_f(N)\otimes_RS\cong Z_f(N_S)$ [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact]; tensoring the exact $N\xrightarrow{\beta_N}Z_f(N)\to H_1(N)\to0$ gives the exact $N_S\xrightarrow{\beta_{N_S}}Z_f(N_S)\to H_1(N)\otimes_RS\to0$ [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact], so $H_1(N)\otimes_RS\cong H_1(N_S)$ with $[x]\otimes1\mapsto[x\otimes1]$, where $x\otimes1=(x_i\otimes1)_i$ (this is 'H_1(N,f)\otimes S=H_1(N\otimes S,f)'). By step 2 and [lem-weil-pbc-torsion-module-flat-base-change-iso], $H_1(N)\to H_1(N)\otimes_RS$, $h\mapsto h\otimes1$, is bijective. Composing: the map $H_1(N)\to H_1(N_S)$, $[x]\mapsto[x\otimes1]$, is bijective; in particular every class of $H_1(N_S)$ is of the form $[x\otimes1]$ with $x\in Z_f(N)$.

source.place: Lemma 05EG, proof, last two sentences: 'As R -> S is flat we have H_1(N, f_•) ⊗_R S = H_1(N ⊗_R S, f_•) ... we have H_1(N, f_•) ⊗_R S = H_1(N, f_•) by Lemma 05E9'

proof.text: The same objects over $S$ for the elements $f_i\in S$: they generate $JS$, and $M_f\otimes_RS\cong M'$, $K_f\otimes_RS\cong K'$, where $M'=S^{\oplus t}/W'$, $\mu':M'\to S$ and $K'=\operatorname{Ker}\mu'$ are the objects of [lem-weil-pbc-cyclic-extension-cocycle] for $A=S$. Indeed, tensoring the exact $R^{\oplus t\times t}\to F\to M_f\to0$ (the first map sending the basis vector of index $(i,j)$ to $f_ie_j-f_je_i$) gives $S^{\oplus t\times t}\to S^{\oplus t}\to M_f\otimes_RS\to0$ exact with the same formula [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact], [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-finite-product], so $M_f\otimes_RS\cong M'$ with $\bar e_i\otimes1\mapsto\bar e_i$ and $\mu\otimes_RS=\mu'$ under $R\otimes_RS=S$; tensoring the exact $0\to K_f\to M_f\xrightarrow{\mu}R$ with the flat $S$ gives $0\to K_f\otimes_RS\to M'\xrightarrow{\mu'}S$ exact [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact], so $K_f\otimes_RS\cong K'$ as submodules of $M'$. For $x\in Z_f(N)$ the map $\hat x\otimes_RS:M_f\otimes_RS\to N_S$ is, under this identification, $\widehat{x\otimes1}:M'\to N_S$ (both send $\bar e_i$ to $x_i\otimes1$). Finally $C_S=(R/J)\otimes_RS\cong S/JS$, $\bar r\otimes s\mapsto\overline{\varphi(r)s}$ [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change] (with the symmetry of the tensor product); fix this isomorphism $\kappa:C_S\to S/JS$.

source.place: Lemma 05EG, proof, second paragraph: the bottom row of the diagram, Ext_S(S/I^nS, N ⊗ S) -> H_1(N ⊗ S, f_•) -> Hom_S(K ⊗ S, N ⊗ S)

proof.text: The given extension: $0\to N_S\xrightarrow{a}T\xrightarrow{\kappa b}S/JS\to0$ is exact. Choose $\tau\in T$ with $\kappa b(\tau)=1\bmod JS$. By [lem-weil-pbc-cyclic-extension-cocycle] (2) for $A=S$, $P=N_S$, the elements $y'_i\in N_S$ with $a(y'_i)=f_i\tau$ form an admissible $y'\in Z_f(N_S)$, and there is an isomorphism $\theta_1:E_f(N_S,y')\to T$ with $\theta_1\iota_{y'}=a$ and $\kappa b\theta_1=\pi_{y'}$. (This is the class of the extension in $\operatorname{Ext}_S(S/I^nS,N\otimes S)\subseteq H_1(N\otimes S,f_\bullet)$, Lemma 05EE.)

source.place: Lemma 05EG, proof, second paragraph: the lower left map Ext_S(S/I^nS, N ⊗ S) -> H_1(N ⊗ S, f_•) of Lemma 05EE

proof.text: By step 3 there are $y\in Z_f(N)$ with $[y\otimes1]=[y']$ in $H_1(N_S)$, i.e. some $m\in N_S$ with $y_i\otimes1=y'_i+f_im$ for all $i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-cyclic-extension-cocycle] (3), applied over $S$ to the admissible $y'$ and the element $-m$, the tuple $y\otimes1$ is admissible and there is an isomorphism $\theta_2:E_f(N_S,y\otimes1)\to E_f(N_S,y')$ commuting with the maps from $N_S$ and to $S/JS$. (This is the surjectivity of the middle vertical arrow $H_1(N,f_\bullet)\to H_1(N\otimes S,f_\bullet)$ in the diagram of 05EG.)

source.place: Lemma 05EG, proof, second paragraph: 'it suffices to prove that the two right vertical arrows are isomorphisms' (middle arrow)

proof.text: $y$ is admissible over $R$, i.e. $u:=\hat y|_{K_f}:K_f\to N$ is $0$. By step 4, $u\otimes_RS:K_f\otimes_RS\to N_S$ is, under $K_f\otimes_RS\cong K'$, the restriction of $\widehat{y\otimes1}$ to $K'$, which is $0$ by step 6. Since $K_f$ is $I$-power torsion (step 1), $u\mapsto u\otimes_RS$ is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_R(K_f,N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_S(K_f\otimes_RS,N_S)$ [lem-weil-pbc-torsion-hom-flat-comparison]; as $0\otimes_RS=0$, $u=0$. (This is the injectivity of the right vertical arrow $\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_S(K\otimes S,N\otimes S)$ in 05EG, which together with the exactness of the rows makes the class $[y]$ come from $\operatorname{Ext}_R(R/I^n,N)$.)

source.place: Lemma 05EG, proof, second paragraph: 'Since K is annihilated by I^n we see that Hom_R(K, N) = Hom_S(K ⊗_R S, N ⊗_R S) by Lemma 05EC', and the diagram chase it concludes

proof.text: Put $E=E_f(N,y)$, $j=\iota_y$, $q=\pi_y$; by step 7 and [lem-weil-pbc-cyclic-extension-cocycle] (1), $0\to N\xrightarrow{j}E\xrightarrow{q}C\to0$ is exact. As $S$ is flat, $0\to N_S\xrightarrow{j_S}E_S\xrightarrow{q_S}C_S\to0$ is exact [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact], [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact], hence so is $0\to N_S\to E_S\xrightarrow{\kappa q_S}S/JS\to0$. Let $e=[(0,1)]\in E$: $q(e)=1\bmod J$ and $f_ie=[(0,f_i)]=[(y_i,0)]=j(y_i)$ because $(y_i,-f_i)\in W_y$. So $e\otimes1\in E_S$ satisfies $\kappa q_S(e\otimes1)=1\bmod JS$ and $f_i(e\otimes1)=j_S(y_i\otimes1)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-cyclic-extension-cocycle] (2) over $S$ (the $x_i$ there are unique, so they are the $y_i\otimes1$), there is an isomorphism $\theta_3:E_f(N_S,y\otimes1)\to E_S$ with $\theta_3\iota_{y\otimes1}=j_S$ and $\kappa q_S\theta_3=\pi_{y\otimes1}$.

source.place: Lemma 05EG, proof, second paragraph: the upper left map Ext_R(R/I^n, N) -> H_1(N, f_•) and the left vertical map Ext_R -> Ext_S (base change of extensions, Homology Lemma 010O)

proof.text: The $S$-linear isomorphism $\theta=\theta_1\theta_2\theta_3^{-1}:E_S\to T$ satisfies $\theta j_S=\theta_1\theta_2\iota_{y\otimes1}=\theta_1\iota_{y'}=a$ and $\kappa b\theta=\pi_{y'}\theta_2\theta_3^{-1}=\pi_{y\otimes1}\theta_3^{-1}=\kappa q_S$, hence $b\theta=q_S$ since $\kappa$ is an isomorphism. So $0\to N\xrightarrow{j}E\xrightarrow{q}C\to0$ and $\theta$ are as required.

split_report.summary: Proof written from Stacks 05EG, second paragraph (the case M = R/I^n), read with 05ED, 05EE, 05EF, 05E9, 05EC; tags checked in tags/tags. The source's Ext_R(R/I^n,N) is the group of extension classes (Homology 010I), not the derived-category Ext of def-pc-ext, so the 05EE row 0 -> Ext -> H_1 -> Hom(K,N) is made explicit on extensions in one new node, lem-weil-pbc-cyclic-extension-cocycle (extension built from an admissible Koszul 1-cycle, every extension of that form, change of cycle by a boundary), and the diagram chase of 05EG is written out: surjectivity of H_1(N) -> H_1(N_S) (flat compatibility of H_1 plus 05EF and 05E9, via lem-weil-pbc-torsion-module-flat-base-change-iso) and injectivity of Hom(K,N) -> Hom(K_S,N_S) (lem-weil-pbc-torsion-hom-flat-comparison, 05EC). 05ED and 05EF are one-line computations, written out in steps 1 and 2. def-pc-ext and lem-weil-pbc-ext-long-exact-first-variable are not used (the sibling nodes of lem-weil-pbc-torsion-extension-flat-descent also work with explicit extensions). Statement unchanged. No Lean on slopmaster2 (grep by id, 05EG/05EE, Koszul).

lean.statement: theorem exists_cyclic_extension_flat_descent {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] (_hflat : (algebraMap R S).Flat) (I : Ideal R) (_hI : I.FG) (_hquot : Function.Bijective (Ideal.quotientMap (I.map (algebraMap R S)) (algebraMap R S) Ideal.le_comap_map)) (n : ℕ) (_hn : 1 ≤ n) {N : Type w} [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] {T : Type x} [AddCommGroup T] [Module S T] (a : S ⊗[R] N →ₗ[S] T) (b : T →ₗ[S] S ⊗[R] (R ⧸ I ^ n)) (_ha : Function.Injective a) (_hab : Function.Exact a b) (_hb : Function.Surjective b) : ∃ (E : Type (max u w)) (_ : AddCommGroup E) (_ : Module R E) (j : N →ₗ[R] E) (q : E →ₗ[R] (R ⧸ I ^ n)), Function.Injective j ∧ Function.Exact j q ∧ Function.Surjective q ∧ ∃ θ : S ⊗[R] E ≃ₗ[S] T, θ.toLinearMap.comp (j.baseChange S) = a ∧ b.comp θ.toLinearMap = q.baseChange S
